questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Trigonometric Expression Using a Common Denominator and the Pythagorean Identity
questions.worked_solution:
We put both terms over a common denominator, and combine the two fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }+\frac{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }+\frac{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta (1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}}{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}}{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )+1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1+1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}{(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =2\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }+\frac{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }=2\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta .
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor ${sin}^{3}⁡x$ from the expression:

$$
{sin}^{5}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x{sin}^{3}⁡x={sin}^{3}⁡x\cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)
$$

Then, we use ${sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{3}⁡x\cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x) & ={sin}^{3}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & ={sin}^{3}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that

$$
{sin}^{5}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x{sin}^{3}⁡x={sin}^{3}⁡x.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Rational Expression Using the Pythagorean Identity
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator:

$$
\frac{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }
$$

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot 1+{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2\cdot \cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }}{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =2\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=2\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta .
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Rational Expression Using the Pythagorean Identity
questions.worked_solution:
First, we factor the denominator:

$$
\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{5}⁡\theta +{sin}^{3}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta }=\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )}
$$

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )} & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{5}⁡\theta +{sin}^{3}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Trigonometric Expression Using a Common Denominator and the Pythagorean Identity
questions.worked_solution:
We put both terms over a common denominator, and combine the two fractions:

$$
\begin{aligned}1+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1}{1}+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{1+{sin}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}{1\cdot (1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{1+{sin}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify using the Pythagorean identity, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1+1}{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2}{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
1+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }=\frac{2}{1+{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }.
$$
